camera: From the lawn at a short end of the bed looking towards the paired water butts. The existing timber planter and the porch glazing run along the left side of the bed.
prompt:
Deliver a SINGLE square 1:1 photorealistic editorial photograph, for location review for John Lennon's UK vegetable gardening book. One exposure, one stage, gardener placing cardboard, no layout, collage, text, number, inset, frame or graphics. The photograph's particular purpose is to recognise this EXACT Cornish home garden bed at the glazed PORCH end. Rebuild the supplied real photograph 1 very faithfully, using its lens direction, spatial relationships and distinctive actual materials. Aim for the effect of visiting the real spot and taking a photograph a few hours earlier. Use the square format by modest widening of the field in the vertical direction, so there is enough room for the man's head and hands as well as the bed; natural working distance. No generic substitute garden.

PHOTO 1 is THE AUTHORITATIVE LOCATION PLATE and camera orientation. Camera on the lawn near one short end observing obliquely along the whole bed. On image LEFT, the row of plain white uPVC glazed porch windows with white base and shallow sill. Directly beneath the real windows runs a SEPARATE, existing wooden planter of weathered two-board-high timber with soil in it; reproduce its modest height, full length and angle. Next to its front face is a VERY narrow strip of pale square/oblong paving, roughly one block across. Beyond this on its LAWN SIDE, the NEW long flat in-ground bed runs PARALLEL alongside the whole porch/planter (not pointed toward the porch). The two adjacent parallel beds must be unambiguous. The NEW bed reaches from near bottom foreground into mid-distance, ending near a pale block wall with ivy on top. Two tall dark grey cylindrical rainwater butts stand side by side at the far end of the WINDOW WALL. The far end and the same long edge of the new bed should line up with these landmarks exactly as in photo 1; do not add a deck, steps, pergola, doors, brick house, elaborate greenhouse, shed, picket fence, flower border or roof. The rear-fence-and-blue-shed view from earlier trials is wrong for this photo; the landmark is specifically the actual white-glazed porch and planter attached to its foot. Windows occupy part of left background, not the whole frame. Keep the open grass on the right.
 
TIME CHANGE ONLY: photo 1 is later the same morning, after compost had been added, but show the earlier CARDBOARD stage here. Photo 2 is the REAL earlier photograph of this exact plot: broad plain worn brown corrugated box panels overlap right on the short grass; some creases, irregular torn corners and small differences of brown, no stencil pattern, printed words, labels, plastic tape or staples. Pale edging pavers are there loosely, one or two holding an edge exactly where plausible, timber ONLY around the established planter, NO timber on the new bed. No compost yet ANYWHERE on the new cardboard bed; the soil inside the separate narrow wooden planter stays as in the real photo. The area around the bed is real green spring lawn, fairly short and recently cut, occasional low weeds or stray blade, with subtle worn patches as in photographs. 
ACTION: At the FRONT RIGHT on adjacent lawn, John kneels low with his knees and boots on the GRASS, torso angled left, quietly concentrating on the cardboard. The far two-thirds down the length already have a believable overlapping patchwork. His hands lower the near edge of a brown flattened carton and press it to overlap the next sheet behind by a generous handspan. Leave a little wedge of the original short grass visible underneath the piece he is setting down. Foreground hands/cardboard contact + bed are the main subject; keep both water butts and some windows legible beside his silhouette. No rake, trowel, compost heap or wheelbarrow at this stage. No posed smile.
Photo 3 is the exact actor, real John as photographed, not a generic bearded gardener. Preserve his appearance, ordinary physique, teal fleece, olive knitted beanie, worn blue jeans and work boots, no microphone, no branding. Use the left-hand view of his face slightly from above as he looks down, receding chin well behind the lower lip, short greying beard tracing the jaw and foreshortening into his collar. A relaxed real kneeling posture with anatomically ordinary arms and hands, natural cloudy Cornish spring light and texture, honest colours, practical documentary photography. Allow enough view of the parallel planter, block strip, cardboard bed, windows and paired water butts to judge the particular location in a single square book photograph.
